To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the coupling between folding and binding is a key factor for the binding of a peptide to a target, (2) the coupling between binding and folding is a key factor in the folding of a peptide, and (3) this coupling can result in a fly-casting effect, where the peptide can bind its target in an accelerated manner, on a timescales of seconds.
“Amphiphilicity, a property of the amino acid sequence of a protein, is a driving force for the folding of a protein into a specific three dimensional structure.”
amphiphilicity can be used as a design principle to control the rate of binding and that the rate of binding is enhanced by the induced folding of a protein upon binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the relationship between the structure of a peptide and its ability to bind a specific target.
the design and synthesis of peptides that fold into a specific secondary structure when they bind to a particular target.
the development of a general model for the folding of disordered proteins that can be used to design peptides with enhanced binding kinetics and selectivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding kinetics of peptides is not enhanced by the induced folding of the peptide, but the binding kinetics of the peptide is enhanced by the induced amphiphilicity of the peptide.
the folding and binding processes are coupled in the sense that they are both dependent on the same set of conditions.
amphiphilic sequences are not always disordered and that amphiphilicity can induce folding and specific biomolecular activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the coupling of folding to amphiphilic binding results in a dramatic enhancement in the binding kinetics, which is due to an increase in the rate of diffusion-limited encounter of the peptide and its target.
the binding kinetics of the designed peptides is enhanced by the presence of an amphiphilic helical segment.

the coupling of the two processes of folding and binding can lead to enhanced binding kinetics, and, in the case of peptides, can result in the ability to fish for amphiphilicity in a solution of similar peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folding and binding processes are coupled in a synergistic manner.
, in order for the “fly-casting effect” to occur, the protein must be amphiphilic.
the folding process of a protein can be coupled to its amphiphilic nature, which can be exploited for the design of peptide-based antimicrobial agents.
